item.title: VP Shadik: Ducsu spent Tk 32L to rid 18 halls of bedbugs
item.description:
Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (DUCSU) has spent Tk32 lakh to eliminate bedbugs from 18 residential halls of Dhaka University, Vice-President Shadik Kayem said on Thursday.
He made the disclosure around 12:45pm while presenting Ducsu’s one-year activities and accountability report at the Ducsu premises on the university campus.
“One of the fundamental crises of our university was bedbugs. Students could not sleep at night because of bedbugs in every hall. After being bitten by bedbugs all night, students could not concentrate on their studies when they went to classes the next day,” Shadik said.
Describing the initiative, he said: “After we were elected, we carried out this work on a priority basis. We have made 18 halls of Dhaka University free of bedbugs by spending around Tk32 lakh. We went room to room and arranged measures to eliminate bedbugs.”
Shadik also described a violence-free campus as Ducsu’s biggest achievement.
“If you ask what the biggest achievement of this Ducsu is, I would say a violence-free campus. After we took responsibility, throughout the entire year, we did not display power over anyone even for a second,” he said.
“If you look at the newspaper columns from the 1990s or earlier, it can be understood that there was no such day when violence did not take place on the campus.”
He said Ducsuhad also organized motorcycle and car driving training, first-aid and spoken English courses, research workshops, and sessions on scholarships and higher education.
Among its transportation initiatives, Ducsu introduced Saturday bus trips, buses for women’s halls and a weekly Dhaka-Comilla bus service, he said.
In healthcare, the union renovated the medical center, organized medical camps and provided free sanitary napkins in five women’s halls, among other initiatives.
Shadik also alleged that the university administration had not provided Ducsu with its allocated budget even after one year.
Despite the administration’s non-cooperation, Ducsu’s committees had carried out more than 1,000 activities, he claimed.

item.title: World Bank unlocks record commercial capital for climate and emerging market infrastructure
item.description:
The World Bank Group announced Thursday that it has mobilized a record-breaking volume of private capital for developing economies over the past fiscal year, marking a major milestone in its ongoing initiative to bridge the widening global development funding gap.
By expanding its guarantee frameworks, refining co-financing structures, and scaling up operations through its private sector arms—including the International Finance Corporation and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency—the institution successfully catalyzed unprecedented levels of commercial investment into high-impact regions and sectors worldwide.
A dominant share of the newly mobilized capital was directed toward climate adaptation, green energy transitions, digital infrastructure, and local healthcare systems in low- and middle-income countries.
To achieve these record numbers, the World Bank Group leaned heavily on streamlined guarantee instruments designed to de-risk emerging market assets, thereby making critical development projects substantially more attractive to institutional investors, pension funds, and international commercial lenders.
Enhanced coordination across all branches of the World Bank Group played a pivotal role in this achievement, allowing the institution to address regulatory bottlenecks more efficiently while deploying unified, market-based solutions.
World Bank Group leadership emphasized that public sector finance and traditional concessionary aid alone are insufficient to meet global climate targets and the Sustainable Development Goals, reiterating that scaling up commercial de-risking mechanisms remains the most viable pathway toward sustaining long-term economic growth across the developing world.

item.title: Gas, power supply improve slightly in Savar, Ashulia, Dhamrai
item.description:
Gas and electricity supplies in industrial and residential areas of Savar, Ashulia and Dhamrai have improved slightly, offering some relief to residents and helping factories resume limited operations. However, the crisis is far from over, with industry stakeholders calling for a further increase in gas supply to restore normal production.
The information was confirmed by sources at the Savar regional office of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited and Dhaka Palli Bidyut Samity-1.
Officials at Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited’s Savar regional office and Dhaka Palli Bidyut Samity-1 confirmed the matter.
During visits to various factories in Savar, Ashulia and Dhamrai on Thursday morning, gas pressure was found to have increased slightly compared with the past few days.
Industry stakeholders said around 1,200 factories operate in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt. Factories with operational boilers and ironing sections, particularly garment units, have seen some improvement in gas supply. However, the pressure remains far below the level required for normal production.
Industry stakeholders said around 1,200 factories operate in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt, with some garment factories seeing improved gas supplies for their boilers and ironing sections. However, gas pressure remains well below the 10-15 PSI required for normal production.
They said gas pressure of 10-15 pounds per square inch (PSI) is required for normal operations. In some areas, pressure had dropped to zero in recent days. Since Wednesday, however, factories have been receiving around 2-3 PSI.
The situation was observed during visits to factories in Radio Colony and Hemayetpur in Savar, and Jamgora, Kathgora, Zirabo, Narsinghpur, Berun, Shimultala, Palashbari, Nishchintapur, Baipayl and Zirani in Ashulia.
Mortuza Ali, director of a garment factory in Savar, told Dhaka Tribune: “We could not operate the boilers and ironing sections for the past few days. Gas supply has increased since Wednesday, allowing us to carry out some work Thursday. However, the supply is still inadequate and needs to be increased further.”
Habibur Rahman, general manager of a garment factory in Dhamrai, said: “The increase allows us to carry out some limited work. Still, it is better than having almost no gas supply.”
Gas pressure improves slightly in residential areas
Gas pressure has also improved slightly in residential areas, although the supply remains inadequate for regular household use.
Ferdausi Sultana, a resident of Savar’s Radio Colony, told Dhaka Tribune: “There was virtually no gas for nearly two months. Some supply has returned, but the pressure is still very low, making cooking difficult.”
Amid the shortage, many residents have turned to alternative cooking arrangements. Sharmin Akter, a resident of College Road in Savar municipality, said: “We are not getting gas at any time of the day or night. So, we have brought in cylinders and are using them for cooking.”
Engineer Abu Saleh Mohammad Khademuddin, the official in charge of Titas Gas’s Ashulia zone, told Dhaka Tribune that the situation had improved somewhat since Wednesday.
“Gas pressure has risen from zero to around 2-3 PSI. We hope the situation will improve further in the coming days,” he said.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Industrial Police-1, who oversees Savar and Ashulia, said he had learned that gas supplies had increased.
“We have no information about any factory suspending operations or facing problems due to the gas shortage,” he said.
Mohiuddin Rubel, founder and CEO of Bangladesh Apparel Voice and a former director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), told Dhaka Tribune that gas supplies had improved and the situation was gradually returning to normal.
“The deadlock has eased,” he said.
Rubel added: “We expect the situation to improve further in line with the government’s commitments. There is no alternative to increasing gas supplies to factories, particularly to keep the industry running.”
Power supply situation
The power supply situation has also improved somewhat, according to Rural Electrification Board sources.
At 2pm on Wednesday, electricity demand at the Savar grid was 42MW, against a supply of 37MW, leaving a 5MW shortfall.
At the Nabinagar grid, demand stood at 90MW, while supply was 78MW, resulting in 12MW of load-shedding.
At the Dhamrai grid, both demand and supply stood at 11MW, while the Mirzapur grid recorded demand and supply of 3MW each. According to the National Load Dispatch Centre (NLDC), neither grid experienced load-shedding.
At the Kabirpur grid, electricity demand stood at 250MW against a supply of 210MW, leaving a 40MW shortfall.
At the Kadda grid, electricity demand stood at 110MW against a supply of 75MW. NLDC imposed 15MW of load-shedding, while feeder shutdowns (F/S) due to busbar overloading accounted for another 20MW.
According to data from the electricity office, the Summit Power Plant supplied 9MW, while United Power supplied no electricity.
On Wednesday, total electricity demand in areas under the jurisdiction of Dhaka Palli Bidyut Samity-1 stood at 515MW, against a total supply of 423MW. The total NLDC load-shedding was 72MW, while 20MW was attributed to overloading.

item.title: Toxic liquor tragedy in Nigeria: 48 dead, 100 hospitalized in Ondo state
item.description:
At least 48 people have died and around 100 others are hospitalized in southern Nigeria after consuming a locally brewed alcoholic drink suspected to contain toxic methanol, officials said Thursday.
Banji Ajaka, commissioner for health in Ondo state, reported that 182 people were affected across the Odigbo and Irele local government areas. He warned that methanol rapidly damages organs, causing kidney failure, blindness and brain damage.
Locals suspect a popular high-proof herbal concoction, known as “Monkey Tail,” was adulterated with methanol. Ondo state police spokesman Abayomi Jimoh said that 15 people have been arrested, including a producer suspected of manufacturing the toxic liquor.
Unregulated, low-cost local alcohol is widely consumed across rural Nigeria. The deaths occur as Nigeria’s National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control enforces a nationwide ban on alcohol sold in sachets and small plastic bottles.

item.title: Two arrested over deaths of 8 Bangladeshis in Mediterranean boat sinking
item.description:
The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested two people for their alleged involvement in a human trafficking syndicate linked to the deaths of eight Bangladeshis in a boat sinking while they were attempting to reach Italy illegally by sea.
The arrestees are Md Rafiqul Islam Rafiq Bagha, 54, and Md Amir Hossain Swapan, 38.
A team of the CID’s Trafficking in Human Beings (THB) unit arrested them on Wednesday (September 16) in the Tekerhat Bazar area of Rajoir upazila in Madaripur.
CID Special Superintendent of Police (Media) Md Sufi Ullah disclosed the information in a press release on Thursday.
According to the release, between December 2023 and February 2024, the syndicate made several attempts to send Bangladeshi nationals from Libya to Italy by sea. During one such attempt, a boat sank off the Tunisian coast, leaving eight Bangladeshis dead.
The victims’ bodies were later repatriated to Bangladesh through government arrangements and handed over to their families. The sole survivor of the incident later disclosed the names and addresses of those allegedly involved in a statement before a court.
The CID investigation found that an organised trafficking syndicate collected large sums of money from victims’ families by promising to send them to Italy legally. The victims were then taken from Libya by motorised trawler and sent toward Italy by sea.
The trawler subsequently sank off the Tunisian coast, killing eight Bangladeshis.
During interrogation, the two arrestees reportedly admitted to collecting money from the family of deceased victim Russel Sheikh, 19, handing it over to other members of the trafficking syndicate and assisting in arrangements to send him abroad, the CID said. The arrestees were produced before a court. A case under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act has been filed against Rafiqul Islam with Rajoir Police Station in Madaripur.
The CID said it is continuing its investigation to identify other people linked to the arrestees, fugitive suspects, local and foreign associates of the trafficking network, and potential victims.
Earlier, two other accused Gurudas Baroi, 45, and Md Motleb Matbar, 68 were arrested and sent to court in connection with the case. The CID urged citizens not to hand over money or passports without proper verification when approached by individuals or organisations offering overseas employment, migration or travel opportunities.
It also advised people to use only government-approved legal channels and verify the credentials of individuals and organisations before making any payments.

item.title: Bangladesh seeks IAEA support to connect RNPP to national grid
item.description:
Bangladesh has sought support from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) to expedite the process of bringing electricity from the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant into the national grid.
The issue was discussed at a meeting between IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi and a Bangladesh delegation led by Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam at the IAEA headquarters in Vienna on Thursday.
The meeting also discussed the peaceful use of nuclear technology, nuclear safety and international cooperation.
Anam expressed gratitude to Grossi for his role in promoting the peaceful uses of nuclear technology and strengthening international cooperation.
The meeting focused on enhancing cooperation between Bangladesh and the IAEA and strengthening the country’s capacity in the peaceful applications of nuclear science and technology through human resource development.
The science minister said Bangladesh has benefited from the IAEA’s technical cooperation program for more than five decades in sectors including health, agriculture, food, water management, industry and energy.
He said Bangladesh recently signed the Country Program Framework (CPF) for 2026–2032, creating new opportunities for technical cooperation in the coming years.
Referring to the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant as a milestone in Bangladesh’s energy security, Anam said the country had made significant progress toward carbon-free electricity generation through fuel loading in Unit 1.
He said the development had opened opportunities to meet growing electricity demand, ensure energy security and address climate change.
Anam said Bangladesh remains committed to maintaining international standards in nuclear safety, security and responsible management.
He noted that Bangladesh’s accession to the Joint Convention on the Safety of Spent Fuel Management and on the Safety of Radioactive Waste Management as the first country in South Asia reflects its commitment to implementing a safe and responsible nuclear program.
Anam also expressed gratitude to Grossi and the IAEA Secretariat leadership for their efforts to advance the “Rays of Hope: Cancer Care for All” initiative.
He said Bangladesh joined the initiative in 2025 and has been working with the IAEA to translate the partnership into programs at the national level.
One of the key priorities is establishing an integrated, one-stop cancer care center to facilitate more coordinated, accessible and patient-centered healthcare services.
Anam said IAEA technical cooperation is important for strengthening capacity, facilitating knowledge exchange and developing a sustainable cancer care system. He emphasized the need to strengthen cooperation under the “Rays of Hope” initiative to expand access to cancer treatment in Bangladesh.
Anam said Bangladesh is looking forward to the IAEA–WHO–IMPACT Review Mission, scheduled for November 2026.
He said the mission would provide an opportunity for an evidence-based assessment of Bangladesh’s national cancer control capacity and help identify practical priorities in various areas of cancer care.
Emphasizing the importance of bringing the benefits of science and technology to the people, Anam said the application of nuclear technology should contribute not only to technological advancement but also to improving quality of life, enhancing climate resilience, increasing agricultural and food productivity, and expanding healthcare services.
He also said creating opportunities for young researchers and scientists, promoting research and innovation, and enhancing knowledge and technological capacity through international cooperation are among Bangladesh’s priorities.
Anam called on the IAEA director general to expand opportunities for international education, training, fellowships and joint research for students, scientists and researchers.
The science and technology minister said the government aims to establish a more integrated, equitable and sustainable cancer care system in Bangladesh so that the benefits of nuclear science and technology can reach those who need them most.
He expressed his commitment to working with the IAEA and its partners to implement the commitments of the “Rays of Hope” initiative.
Anam also called for further international cooperation through the IAEA in promoting the peaceful uses of nuclear technology, strengthening nuclear safety and advancing sustainable development.
Among those present at the meeting were Md Anowar Hossain, secretary, Ministry of Science and Technology; Tofique Hasan, ambassador and permanent representative of Bangladesh to the United Nations and other international organizations in Vienna; Dr M Moinul Islam, chairman, Bangladesh Atomic Energy Commission; and Sheikh Mohammad Towhidul Islam, joint secretary of the science ministry.

item.title: RMG exports to EU dip 13.65% in 7 months
item.description:
Bangladesh’s readymade garment (RMG) exports to the European Union declined by 13.65% year-on-year to 10.37 billion euros in January-July of 2026.
In the mentioned period, the EU imported apparel worth 51.61 billion euros, which saw a decline of 5.10% from 54.39 billion euros a year earlier, according to Eurostat data.
Although Bangladesh remained the EU’s second-largest apparel supplier after China, the gap widened further as China posted growth in an otherwise contracting market, showed data compiled by Bangladesh Apparel Voice.
Among the major suppliers, Bangladesh recorded the sharpest decline. Exporters attributed the decline to fall in demands, intensifying competition and domestic energy crisis.
In terms of volume, Bangladesh shipped 751.91 million kilograms of apparel to the EU in the January-July period of 2026, down 5.66% from 796.98 million kilograms recorded in the same period of 2025.
The steeper fall in value compared with volume indicates that Bangladeshi exporters received significantly lower unit prices during the period.
Moreover, the average unit price of Bangladeshi apparel on the EU market stood at 13.80 euros a kilogram, which was 8.47% lower than the 15.07 euros recorded in January-July of 2025.
Bangladesh’s unit price also remained the second lowest among the major suppliers after Pakistan’s 10.77 euros, against the EU average of 19.84 euros a kilogram.
By comparison, Vietnam’s unit price rose 11.76% to 29.00 euros and Cambodia’s 7.86% to 18.67 euros, while China’s edged down 2.18% to 20.20 euros.
Among major apparel exporters, China’s apparel exports to the EU rose 1.89% to 16.42 billion euros from 16.12 billion euros, making it the only major supplier apart from Vietnam to record growth during the period.
Among the other major suppliers, Turkey’s apparel exports to the EU fell 13.32% to 4.38 billion euros in the first six months of 2026 from 5.06 billion euros in the same period of 2025, while India’s declined 12.24% to 2.74 billion euros from 3.13 billion euros.
Cambodia’s shipments dropped 6.69% to 2.34 billion euros from 2.51 billion euros and Pakistan’s fell 11.81% to 1.96 billion euros from 2.22 billion euros.
Vietnam’s exports increased by 3.92% to 2.55 billion euros from 2.46 billion euros, taking it past Cambodia to become the EU’s fifth-largest apparel supplier during the period.
Exporters also urged adequate policy supports, like the competitors, to remain competitive on the EU markets, along with focus on market and product diversification, innovation and research.
Bangladesh’s RMG exports to the European Union reached 19.41 billion euros in 2025, witnessing a positive growth of 5.97% from 18.31 billion euros earned in 2024.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,046 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Thursday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,046 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all two latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With these, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 946, while confirmed deaths from measles have remained the same at 100.
A total of 1,282 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to176,480
Meanwhile, 61 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 20,343
Since March 15 this year, a total of 155,602 patients with measles-like symptoms have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 149,540 have recovered, according to DGHS data.

item.title: Passengers fight mid-air aboard Biman flight, video goes viral
item.description:
A video showing two passengers fighting mid-air aboard a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight has gone viral on social media.
The flight was travelling from London to Bangladesh when the two passengers reportedly got into a heated argument that escalated into a physical altercation, causing panic among fellow passengers, including children and elderly people.
The video shows the two men arguing before exchanging blows. At one point, one passenger’s T-shirt was torn during the scuffle. As the situation escalated, cabin crew members and other passengers intervened and tried to separate the two men.
Biman Bangladesh Airlines General Manager (Public Relations) Mahbubuddin Ahmed told Dhaka Tribune that he was not yet aware of the incident.
“I am not aware of the matter yet. I am looking into it,” he said.

item.title: EC Md Sanaullah: Timeframe for UP election to be reviewed
item.description:
The Election Commission will review the timeframe for holding Union Parishad elections in phases before finalizing the election schedule, said Election Commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah on Thursday.
“We’ll review requests from different ministries and agencies concerned before finalizing the schedule for the Union Parishad elections. But everyone agreed that we need to finish the elections by June 6 next year,” he said.
The commissioner made the remarks while briefing reporters after an interministerial preparatory meeting on a parliamentary by-election and local government elections at Nirbachan Bhaban in the city.
The meeting began at 2:30pm with Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin in the chair.
Senior representatives from more than 20 ministries and divisions, including the Armed Forces Division, law enforcement and intelligence agencies attended the meeting.
Sanaullah said the EC received a number of requests from the participants regarding the timing of the elections.
They requested us to consider that the annual examinations in schools will be held throughout November and December next, he said.
The commissioner said the EC would have some scope in January to arrange the local government elections and another window between the SSC and HSC examinations.
He said the SSC examinations will be held after Ramadan, while the HSC examinations will be held after June 6.
Regarding the tentative dates announced on Monday for the seven-phase UP elections, Sanaullah said, “We earlier said we will finalize the schedule after the September 17 meeting.”
Four election commissioners—Abdur Rahmanel Mashud, Begum Tahmida Ahmad, Anwarul Islam Sarker and Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah—and EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed were present at the meeting.
The Thakurgaon-1 by-election is scheduled to be held on October 29.
On Monday, the EC announced tentative dates for holding the countrywide Union Parishad elections in seven phases with the first phase planned for November 12.
However, two ministers and the prime minister’s advisers on Tuesday said the government was unaware of the tentative dates before the EC announced them.

item.title: Lawyer argues own bail before being sent to jail in anti-terrorism case
item.description:
Advocate Abul Bashar, a former executive committee member of the Dhaka Bar Association, argued his own bail petition before a Dhaka court on Thursday after the judge asked whether he had a lawyer, but was ultimately sent to jail in an anti-terrorism case filed with Pallabi police station.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mahbub Alam passed the order following an application by the investigation officer. SI Saiful Islam of the prosecution department confirmed the matter.
Bashar was produced before the court at noon and kept in the lockup of the Dhaka CMM Court. His bail hearing began around 2pm, with his lawyers applying to hold the hearing in his presence.
At around 3:45pm, Bashar was brought into the courtroom, which became crowded with pro-Awami League lawyers taking selfies and making videos. As the noise increased, security was tightened and several police personnel were deployed.
Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruk Faruqi then entered with state lawyers and pro-BNP lawyers.
“There is no environment for the hearing of the case. There needs to be an environment for the hearing. The hearing of the case will begin after that,” Faruqi told the pro-Awami League lawyers.
He asked everyone except those who had submitted vakalatnama to leave. Pro-Awami League lawyer Saiful Islam Sohag said: “The environment of the court will remain calm.”
At 4:30pm, the judge took the bench and asked whether Bashar had a lawyer. Standing in the dock, Bashar said he would conduct the hearing himself, submitted a vakalatnama and began his arguments.
Bashar said that at around 10:30pm on Wednesday, while returning home through Pallabi’s Section 11, he stopped at a pharmacy to buy milk for his 22-month-old child. As he had no money, he was going to withdraw money from bKash when three or four people blocked and beat him over an argument about drugs. Local people rescued him and called 999.
“I became a lawyer in 2016. I have never behaved disrespectfully with anyone. I regularly practise in court. I want justice from you [the judge],” he said.
Omar Faruk Faruqi opposed bail, alleging Bashar was identified by local people as being involved in a procession where slogans were chanted against the government and fugitive former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.
Bashar said the allegation could be checked through videos, screenshots and location data, adding that “they did not find anything of any kind against me.”
Faruqi later said the public identified and handed Bashar over to police before police identified him.
The court rejected Bashar’s bail petition and ordered him sent to jail.
According to the case details, Awami League leaders and activists brought out a procession in the Pallabi metro rail area at around 6:30am on July 31. SI Sohan Molla of Pallabi police station filed the anti-terrorism case that day. Bashar was detained by people in Pallabi’s Section 12 around 10:30pm Wednesday and later shown arrested in the case.
Pallabi police station SI Salahuddin Al-Mamun sought an order to keep him in jail.

item.title: Over 50 injured in clash over football match in Patuakhali
item.description:
More than 50 people were injured in a clash between two groups over a football match in Galachipa upazila of Patuakhali on Thursday.
According to locals and police, a quarterfinal match between South Kalikapur United and Mativanga Challenge XI was underway at the Kalikapur Government Primary School ground under Sadar union.
About 10 minutes before the end of the match around 5:30pm, South Kalikapur scored a goal, prompting the opposing team to allege a foul and argue with the referee.
At one stage, an altercation broke out between players of the two teams and soon turned into a clash. Local people later joined the fray.
The clash later spread across the upazila headquarters, with those involved taking to the streets carrying locally made weapons, according to locals.
Over 50 people from both groups were injured during the melee. They received treatment at various hospitals.
Later, police brought the situation under control, said Galachipa Police Station Officer-in-Charge Moniruzzaman.
He said they arrested one person in connection with the incident.

Woman dies after being pushed during family dispute in Basabo
item.description:
A 48-year-old woman has succumbed to head injuries she sustained allegedly after being pushed during a family dispute involving her stepbrother and his wife in the capital's Basabo area.
The deceased was identified as Afroza Irene, daughter of Anwar Ullah of Ekhlaspur village in Faridganj upazila of Chandpur. She lived with her husband Belal Hossain in a rented house in Ahmedbagh area of Basabo.
Police recovered the body from Mugda Medical College Hospital on Wednesday afternoon and sent it to Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue on Thursday morning for an autopsy.
According to police and family sources, an altercation broke out between Afroza, her stepbrother Babu, and his wife Fatema at their Basabo residence at around 10pm on Monday over family matters.
At one point, Babu and Fatema forcefully pushed Afroza, causing her to fall onto bricks and sustain severe head injuries.
Family members took her to Mugda Medical College Hospital, where she succumbed to her injuries on Wednesday afternoon.

item.title: Three killed in Dhamrai road crash
item.description:
Three people were killed when a pickup collided with a CNG-run auto-rickshaw on Kalampur-Saturia-Nagpur Road in Dhamrai upazila of Dhaka on Thursday.
The deceased were identified as Akhi Akter, daughter of Abul Hossain of Isapur village, Zakaria Hossain, son of Jashim Uddin of Sadar upazila in Tangail district, and Jewel Hossain, driver of the auto-rickshaw.
Ilias Hossain, in-charge of Kawalipara Bazar police camp, said the two vehicles collided at Nandeshwari in the evening.
Following the collision, the three-wheeler got twisted and plunged into the roadside ditch, leaving two people dead on the spot and its driver injured.
Later, the injured was taken to Saturia Upazila Health Complex in Manikganj district, where doctors declared him dead.

item.title: Mosquito Killing Week begins at KUET
item.description:
Khulna University of Engineering and Technology (KUET) has launched a Mosquito Killing Week to prevent mosquito-borne diseases and maintain a healthy campus environment.
KUET Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Muhammad Masud inaugurated the Mosquito Killing Week 2026 on Thursday.
Speaking at the inauguration, the vice-chancellor stressed the importance of regular mosquito control and cleanliness drives alongside greater awareness and responsible participation by teachers, officials, employees and students.
He urged everyone to work together to keep the campus clean and destroy mosquito breeding grounds.
The campaign will continue from September 17 to 23, covering residential halls, academic and administrative buildings, roads, drains, waterlogged areas and other parts of the campus.
The university said the initiative would strengthen mosquito control measures and help maintain a clean and healthy campus environment.
Prof Dr Mohammad Abu Yusuf, chairman of the university’s Security Committee and dean of the Faculty of Science and Humanities, also spoke at the program.
Deans of various faculties, institute directors, the acting registrar, heads of departments, directors, branch heads, teachers, officials and employees attended the event.

item.title: Five killed as Yemen’s Houthis, govt, Saudi Arabia trade strikes
item.description:
Attacks attributed to the Houthis, the Yemeni government and its Saudi backers killed at least five people on Thursday, as fighting rocked the Arabian Peninsula after the Iran-backed group made lightning gains in a fresh offensive.
The three sides have been locked in increasingly violent exchanges since Yemen’s civil war flared back to life, with Saudi Arabia accusing the Houthis of firing at the holy city of Mecca this week.
On Thursday, the Houthis said “Saudi enemy warplanes targeted three telecommunications towers” in Taiz province, with one civilian killed and another injured in strikes on the town of Abs, Almasirah television said.
The Houthi-backed outlet later reported that “three children were killed and several Yemeni nationals were injured in strikes by the Saudi-backed mercenaries,” a reference to the country’s internationally recognized government.
Saudi Arabia’s civil defense agency, meanwhile, reported casualties caused by debris from an intercepted Houthi drone in an area east of Mecca.
“The fall of shrapnel from a downed drone in Taif governorate resulted in one death, two injuries, and material damage to several buildings and vehicles,” the agency said in a statement posted on social media, adding that the person killed was a Yemeni national.
The death was the first reported in Saudi Arabia since the recent fighting flared.
Images posted by Saudi state media showed windows in cars and shop fronts shattered by the shrapnel, with nearby buildings also damaged.
The incidents come a day after Riyadh accused the Houthis of launching a “cowardly” attack targeting Islam’s holy city of Mecca, a claim they denied.
The Houthis have been reporting dozens of daily Saudi strikes since they launched their new offensive and seized control of strategic coastal areas overlooking the Red Sea’s Bab al-Mandab Strait from government forces.
With Iran already throttling the Strait of Hormuz since the outbreak of the wider Middle East war, their Yemeni allies’ latest gains cement their hold on the other main shipping corridor for Gulf oil and gas.
The route had been especially important to Saudi Arabia, the world’s top crude exporter, which had used a pipeline to bypass the Hormuz and send oil to the Red Sea, which links Europe and Asia via the Suez Canal.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce between the Houthis and the government fell apart after the group allowed an Iranian plane to land in the capital Sanaa in defiance of Riyadh’s control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
They also announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began striking its ships and territory.
The conflict in the Arabian Peninsula’s poorest country has forced more than 100,000 people to flee their homes, according to the United Nations.

item.title: Macron hosts Lebanon security talks as UN mission nears end
item.description:
The leaders of France, Lebanon and Jordan on Thursday met in Paris to discuss international support for the cash-strapped Lebanese army and the creation of a new force to succeed a longstanding UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon.
French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and King Abdullah II of Jordan.
They were joined by chiefs of defense staff from Lebanon, Jordan, France, Britain and Italy, as well as top US and Saudi officials, a French military source said.
The talks come as the mandate of the United Nations Interim Force In Lebanon (Unifil) ends this year after almost half a century of operations dating back to the Israeli invasion of 1978.
Last year, the UN Security Council, under US pressure, decided to end Unifil’s mandate on December 31, 2026.
France and Italy have said they want to set up a multinational coalition to succeed Unifil.
Lebanon will be one of key issues on the agenda as world leaders gather for the UN General Assembly in New York next week.
“The aim for the participants is to jointly assess what the Lebanese armed forces need,” the French military source said, referring to the Paris talks.
“The goal is to find realistic and effective solutions.”
Aoun told AFP this week that Lebanon wanted a new force, European or otherwise, to prevent a security vacuum after the UN peacekeepers leave south Lebanon.
During bilateral talks earlier Thursday, Macron and Aoun discussed “progress in drafting proposals for the Security Council regarding the future of the international presence in southern Lebanon,” the Lebanese presidency said.
The two leaders also discussed Israeli attacks against Lebanese villages and towns and efforts to halt them, the presidency added.
Israel and the United States attacked Iran in February, sparking a war that has spread across the Middle East.
Lebanese militant group Hezbollah dragged Lebanon into the wider conflict when it fired rockets at Israel in solidarity with the Tehran government.
Israel attacked south Lebanon and its forces continue to occupy what it calls a “security zone,” a stretch of Lebanese territory about 10 kilometers (six miles) deep along the border.
In June, Israel and Lebanon signed a US-sponsored framework agreement that involves the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon’s south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region.
Violence declined following the June agreement and a wider US-Iran deal, but Israel has pressed its attacks on Lebanon.
The French presidency said the aim of the Paris talks was to review a Lebanese armed forces deployment plan based on a “clear, credible and realistic” framework.
Paris said it wanted this as a prerequisite for what it hopes will be “robust” international support, whether in the form of financial assistance, equipment or training.
The poorly equipped Lebanese forces have struggled to carry out their mission of disarming Hezbollah in the south, which is a key condition for Israel’s withdrawal from southern Lebanon.
Aoun has reiterated his determination to disarm Hezbollah, but “without a confrontation.”
The Lebanese president has also called on Europeans, Americans and Arab nations to support the Lebanese army.
Unifil, which must end by the end of the year, has just under 7,500 peacekeepers from 46 countries.
On Thursday, Aoun also stressed the importance of organizing a conference on the reconstruction of Lebanon, which Macron had hoped to hold alongside the conference aimed at supporting the Lebanese armed forces.
The outbreak of war in the spring postponed both gatherings indefinitely.
Lebanon has been dealing with an unprecedented financial crisis since 2019 and was still reeling from the 2024 Israel-Hezbollah war when the Iran-backed group drew it into the Middle East conflict in March.

item.title: Turkiye proposes Russia-Ukraine deal to end Black Sea shipping attacks
item.description:
Turkiye has sent a proposal to Russia and Ukraine that would end attacks on civilian ships in the Black Sea, a Turkish diplomat told AFP on Thursday.
The move follows a sharp uptick in attacks in the Black Sea, which has seen at least 25 Turkish-owned vessels hit since late June, industry figures show.
“We have shared a text of a memorandum, a draft text, with the Russians and the Ukrainians to come up with a solution to those strikes taking place in the Black Sea,” the diplomat said.
He said the proposal was “inspired by” the grain corridor mechanism -- a 2022 deal brokered by Turkiye and the UN to grant safe passage for Ukrainian grain to be exported via the Black Sea without risk of attack.
Although Russia pulled out a year later, Ukraine set up an alternative path via a shipping route that hugs the coast of Romania and Bulgaria.
“In that mechanism, there is maybe a four- or five-mile gap where the Ukrainian ship has to leave the national territorial waters and travel in international waters, which is the risky part,” he explained.
“So our offer is also inspired by this.”

item.title: World’s water cycle becoming more unpredictable, UN warns
item.description:
The planet’s water cycle is becoming increasingly erratic, swinging between too little and too much, the United Nations warned Thursday, with an unprecedented El Nino expected to exacerbate the long-term trend.
Last year was among the driest for the world’s rivers in over three decades, the UN’s World Meteorological Organization said in a report.
In 2025 -- one of the warmest years on record -- glaciers also shrank across all regions, even as groundwater levels in many parts of the world are in multi-year decline, it found.
Overall, the WMO’s annual State of Global Water Resources report showed that the Earth’s freshwater storage -- the total amount of water stored in groundwater, lakes and rivers, soil moisture, vegetation and ice and snow -- continued a decade-long decline.
Some elements of the water cycle change rapidly -- like precipitation, river flow and soil moisture, responding to weather within days or weeks.
WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo voiced particular concern about the decline in “slow reserves,” like groundwater and glaciers, which she said had traditionally served as the planet’s “savings account.”
They have served as “a buffer that absorbs bad years so that a single drought or a single dry season does not translate directly into a water crisis,” she told reporters.
Now, “we are depleting that savings account,” she warned. “We are spending our reserves.”
Glaciers have also been shrinking at a precipitous rate, with 2025 marking the fourth consecutive year where they shed significant ice mass across all regions.
Between 2023 and 2025, the report estimated that glaciers lost a cumulative global glacier mass of 1,400 gigatons of water -- roughly equal to the water required to fill 560 million Olympic-sized swimming pools, or about a third of the world’s annual freshwater withdrawals.
“Groundwater tells a similar story: nearly two-thirds of monitored wells worldwide showed conditions outside the historical norm in 2025,” Saulo said.
She highlighted that this was happening in parallel with “more water-related disasters.”
In particular, she pointed to the current El Nino pattern, which is expected to be the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.
El Nino is the warm phase of a natural climate cycle that occurs every two to seven years and is characterised by above average ocean temperatures across the Pacific, and brings worldwide changes in winds and rainfall patterns and erratic weather.
“The strengthening El Nino will increase the risk of drought in some areas, and flooding in others,” Saulo cautioned.
Already before El Nino hit, rivers worldwide were showing “abnormal” flows, WMO said, with 2025 among the three driest years for rivers in 35 years.
For a seventh year in a row, the number of river basins globally experiencing “normal” conditions were in a clear minority in 2025.
Only around 36 percent saw normal flows, while an equal percentage saw below-normal discharge conditions and 21 percent were above normal, the report found.
The WMO stressed the importance of good data to map the developments in the water cycle, warning that significant gaps remained in hard-hit areas.
“Weather respects no borders, and this is especially true for water,” Saulo said, arguing for the importance of “shared data, shared standards and shared early warnings.”
“A river basin is fed by water upstream, often in another country,” she pointed out.
And “a glacier disaster in one country can lead to devastation in another as we saw with the recent tragedy of China and Nepal.”

Notes From a Hungry Homeland
item.description:
How brave a soul must be to love through poverty,
in a country where the flag frays a little more each season,
stitched by hope yet torn by hungry hands and restless histories.
Streets remember promises louder than prayers,
and still the heart dares to choose love over survival.
My soul refuses sleep unless it witnesses spring arriving softly,
blossoms opening like wounds learning forgiveness,
unless it walks through the storm-swollen nights of July
where thunder writes grief across a dusky sky
and rain falls like unfinished confessions.
What is love here, if not endurance?
What is devotion, if not staying when leaving would be easier?
Through winter’s pale and trembling daze
I remain, a poor man with pockets full of longing—
learning that love is not abundance but persistence,
not warmth alone but the courage to shiver beside another soul.
So I must love through emptiness, through broken seasons,
through a homeland that forgets how gently hearts can live,
because only by loving without certainty, without wealth, without shelter,
do I begin, slowly and painfully,
to understand you.

Foreign credit card transactions: 18% spent in the US
item.description:
The trend of Bangladeshis using credit cards abroad has increased, with the most significant rise recorded in the United States.
According to the latest data from Bangladesh Bank, Bangladeshi credit cardholders spent a total of Tk525.90 crore abroad in July this year.
This represents a 9.71% increase compared to the same period last year.
Notably, 17.71% of all international credit card transactions occurred in the US alone—meaning nearly Tk18 out of every Tk100 spent overseas went to the US.
However, Bangladesh Bank's updated report reveals a 5.05% drop in total foreign credit card spending in July compared to June's figure of Tk552.70 crore.
Country-wise, Thailand ranked second after the US in July, accounting for 11.68% of total international transactions.
This was followed by the UK (10.35%), Singapore (7.54%), India (6.69%), and Malaysia (6.55%). Canada accounted for 4.74%, the Netherlands 4.17%, China 4.01%, and Australia 3.49%.
The bulk of foreign credit card expenditure went toward purchasing goods and services.
In July, department stores accounted for 31.33% of total transactions.
Retail outlet services followed at 17.18%, transportation at 12.50%, medicine/pharmacies at 11.44%, clothing stores at 7.96%, and business services at 7.29%.
Bank officials attributed the growth in foreign card usage to increased overseas travel and an improved dollar supply.
Foreign travel declined during the political instability of 2024. However, card-based international transactions have rebounded as travel for medical, educational, and leisure purposes has picked up.
Additionally, improved dollar availability in banks has normalized transaction flows.
Card usage limits abroad have also expanded.
Bangladesh Bank previously allowed citizens to spend up to $12,000 annually via credit cards overseas, a limit that was recently raised to $18,000.
The US also dominated foreign spending via debit and prepaid cards, accounting for 13.25% of overseas debit card usage and 16.37% of prepaid card usage in July.
Across all three card types combined, the US accounted for 15.81% of total foreign spending.
Meanwhile, domestic credit card usage surged by 40.24% in July. Industry experts point to high inflation as a primary driver.
Former Bangladesh Bank chief economist Mustafa K. Mujeri noted that persistent inflationary pressure has led many individuals to rely on credit cards for temporary relief—warning, however, that debt-driven spending could pose major future risks.
According to Bangladesh Bank, the total number of debit, credit, and prepaid cards jumped 97% between August 2021 and July this year, while overall card transactions grew by 108% over the same period.
By the end of July, Bangladesh had 46.3 million debit cards, 2.7 million credit cards, and 9.1 million prepaid cards in circulation.

item.title: BSEC to introduce direct listing
item.description:
The Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission is going to introduce direct listing option as an alternative to IPOs, allowing established companies of the country to be listed in the capital market through offloading shares held by company directors.
Direct listing offers an alternative avenue for established companies—which do not need to raise new capital for business expansion or operations but wish to list on the stock market—to be listed through the offloading of shares by existing shareholders.
The BSEC announced the rule in a press release issued on Wednesday.
The commission has drafted the ‘Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (Direct Listing of Securities on Stock Exchanges) Rules, 2026’ and published it for public comments. The rules are expected to be finalized and gazetted soon.
Under the proposed system, companies will not raise fresh capital by issuing new shares. Instead, existing shareholders will offload their shares to facilitate the listing, offering an alternative route for established companies that do not need additional funds for operations or expansion.
The BSEC notes that this system will create opportunities to increase the participation of new and capable companies in the stock market.
Simultaneously, it will provide existing shareholders with the opportunity to offload their shares, potentially enhancing the depth and scope of the stock market.
According to the new rule, specific eligibility criteria must be met for direct listing. Only companies that qualify under the proposed rules will be able to apply for listing through this system.
However, the IPO route also remains available for companies seeking to raise new capital. Companies currently interested in raising capital from the stock market via an IPO can apply in accordance with the existing “Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission (Public Issue of Equity Securities) Rules, 2025.”

item.title: BB instructs banks, MFS providers to block payments to illegal loan apps
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has instructed banks, mobile financial service (MFS) providers and other payment service providers (PSPs) to immediately suspend payment services to operators of mobile apps involved in unauthorized online lending.
The banking regulator also requested the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC) and other relevant authorities to remove mobile apps involved in unauthorized online lending from online platforms, including the Google Play Store, and permanently stop their use and operation.
The central bank issued separate letters to those authorities recently.
BB also asked banks to take effective measures to raise public awareness against such apps and report the steps taken to its Payment Systems Supervision Department.
In the letter, BB said some mobile apps operating on online platforms are providing loans at high interest rates, exposing borrowers to financial losses and harassment.
It said such apps can gain access to users’ phone contacts, personal and sensitive information, photos, videos and text messages without their knowledge.
Borrowers who fail to repay loans may then face blackmail, threats to publish sensitive information and photographs on social media, and other forms of harassment, it added.
Citing Section 15(2) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024, Bangladesh Bank said no person can operate an online or offline platform involving investment collection, lending, fund custody or financial transactions without its approval.
As the lending activities of the identified apps are being conducted without Bangladesh Bank approval, they are illegal and constitute a punishable offence under Section 37(1) of the law, it said.
The central bank warned that operators of such apps are directly involved in a punishable offence. It also said scheduled banks, MFSs, digital financial service and payment service provider institutions that facilitate transactions related to such lending could be considered involved in the offence as financial transaction channels.
Under Section 19(4) of the law, Bangladesh Bank therefore directed all institutions and individuals concerned, including the operators of the identified apps listed in an attachment, to immediately stop providing payment services to them.
Earlier, the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit warned the public against taking loans through unauthorized mobile apps and digital platforms and named 30 illegal apps involved in extortion, data theft and financial fraud.
The BFIU identified 30 unauthoriszd apps, including Sathi Loan, Pop Cash, FinCash, Quick Loan, Quick Taka, Dhaka Fin, LoanVibe, Dost Loan, Taka Cash Loan, KWANZA Loan, SSH Money, LoanBuddy, Cash-Hora, Alo Cash, Fast Loan, Easy Taka, Dhorjo Loan, Fin Dot Do, BongoCash, Asha Loan, Subidha Loan, Smart Loan BD, Online Loan BD, City Online Loan, BD Shohoj Loan, Cash Loan, Sonali, Loan Haat and Taka Nao.

item.title: Before you watch Netflix's ‘Monster’: Let’s talk about the real Lizzie Borden murder case
item.description:
For three seasons, Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan's "Monster" anthology has asked audiences to sit uncomfortably close to men who kill--Jeffrey Dahmer, the Menendez brothers, and Ed Gein. On September 17, that formula breaks.
"Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story," the fourth season of the anthology, drops all eight episodes at once on Netflix, and for the first time, the killer at the centre of the frame is a woman. And Ella Beatty stars as Lizzie Borden.
The case itself needs no introduction to true-crime devotees, but for the uninitiated: Lizzie Borden was accused of the axe murders of her father and stepmother in Fall River, Massachusetts, in 1892. It is still one of the most enduringly debated criminal cases in American history.
Before Netflix's version takes its liberties, here's the actual case "Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story" is built on.
And it all goes back to the morning of August 4, 1892.
Andrew and Abby Borden were found dead in the home they shared with Lizzie and her older sister Emma in Fall River, Massachusetts. Andrew's body was discovered on a sitting-room couch, his head and face struck repeatedly with an axe or hatchet.
Police then found Abby's body upstairs. She was also brutally murdered earlier that same morning.
Besides Lizzie, the only other person in the house was the family's maid, Bridget Sullivan. And that made Lizzie the prime suspect almost immediately. By her own account, she'd been in the barn eating pears before finding her father's body. She said she didn't go looking for her stepmother afterward.
This is the detail most adaptations gloss over: there was no physical evidence tying Lizzie to the crime. No murder weapon was ever conclusively identified, and Lizzie had no blood on her despite the killings happening in a window of roughly fifteen minutes.
Even police testimony about the suspected hatchet contradicted itself at trial. Motive was murky, too. The Bordens were wealthy; Lizzie and Emma stood to inherit.
Lizzie reportedly had a strained relationship with her stepmother, but none of it was ever proven. A druggist was prepared to testify that a Borden woman had once tried to buy poison and been refused. The court excluded that testimony entirely.
Lizzie was arrested and charged on August 11, 1892, a week after the bodies were found. Her inconsistent answers under police questioning, and her strikingly composed demeanor throughout, did little to help her in the court of public opinion even before the trial began.
The trial opened on June 5, 1893, in New Bedford, with defense attorneys George D. Robinson (a former Massachusetts governor) and Andrew Jennings representing Lizzie against prosecutors Hosea Knowlton and William H. Moody. Newspapers covered it obsessively, and public opinion split hard between "vengeful harpy" and "wrongly accused Christian woman."
The turning point came from the bench. Judge Justin Dewey ruled that Lizzie's confused statements to police couldn't be used at trial. The reason being she’d made them without a lawyer present.
Without that testimony or the poison evidence, prosecutors leaned almost entirely on circumstantial argument. The case's most theatrical moment came when the district attorney, mid-closing-argument, dropped Lizzie's dress onto the prosecution table, revealing her parents' actual skulls kept as evidence.
Lizzie reportedly fainted at the sight, swinging courtroom sympathy sharply her way.
On June 20, 1893, an all-male, all-white, Protestant jury deliberated for roughly 90 minutes before returning a verdict of not guilty. By most historical accounts, jurors simply couldn't accept that a respectable, church-going woman of Lizzie's standing was capable of such violence. The murders remain officially unsolved.
Lizzie was ostracized in Fall River, though she never left town. She and Emma bought a fourteen-room house they named Maplecroft, where Lizzie, who began going by "Lizbeth," lived a largely private life. She started traveling to Boston, New York, and Washington and formed a close friendship with stage actress Nance O'Neil. She and Emma eventually had a falling out. Lizzie died in 1927 at age 66, still shadowed by suspicion.
No weapon, no confession, no alternate suspect ever charged. That vacuum is exactly what period dramas like "Monster" are built to fill, reading motive and repression into gaps the record never closed.
Whatever liberties the show takes, the core facts remain: two people were killed with a hatchet on a hot August morning. A woman was tried and acquitted on evidence too thin to convict but too suspicious to fully clear her.

item.title: Health ministry seeks content creators’ support to fight dengue
item.description:
State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit has called on popular content creators to help raise awareness about dengue and promote behavioral change, saying digital content can complement medical measures to prevent infections and deaths.
He made the call at an exchange meeting with leading content creators and social media influencers at the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s conference room on Thursday.
The meeting discussed engaging popular digital content creators in dengue prevention to promote positive behavioral changes beyond conventional government awareness campaigns.
A coordinated three-month action plan for dengue prevention and public health protection was also discussed at the meeting.
Muhit said the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and hospitals are preparing to provide dengue treatment.
He said 3,000 doctors are receiving refresher training, while steps are being taken to ensure adequate supplies of saline and keep the necessary number of hospital beds ready.
However, the state minister said strengthening treatment alone would not be enough to reduce dengue infections and deaths.
